title: "Usage"
toc: true
number-sections: false
---

All use cases are covered by subcommands of the `ai4copsec-restapi` command
line tool. By default, settings are read from a `.env` file in the current
working directory; every subcommand also accepts `--env-file <filename>` to
point at a specific configuration.

## Starting the API

```bash
ai4copsec-restapi start --port=12000
```

The API is then reachable on port 12000, with the OpenAPI docs at:

```
http://127.0.0.1:12000/api/v1/docs
```

## Running with SSL

Get or create a certificate and pass it to `start`:

```bash
openssl req -nodes -new -x509 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 \
    -subj "/C=countrycode/ST=state/L=city/O=Organization Name/OU=Unit Name/CN=cname/emailAddress=creator@yourdomain"

ai4copsec-restapi start --reload --port 12000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --ssl-keyfile key.pem --ssl-certfile cert.pem
```

## Enabling OAuth

By default, Bearer-token authentication is disabled. To enable it, configure
the API according to your identity provider - the setup has been
developed/tested with Keycloak. Add the following to your `.env` file:

```
AI4COPSEC_RESTAPI_OAUTH_REQUIRED=true
AI4COPSEC_RESTAPI_OAUTH_URL="http://ai4copsec.identity-provider.org"
AI4COPSEC_RESTAPI_OAUTH_REALM="ai4copsec-realm"
```

## Technological brick endpoints

Each technological brick exposes the same three-route shape under
`/api/v1/technological_brick/<brick>/`:

| Brick | Prefix | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ship/oil-spill detection | `sod` | `description`, `algorithms`, `detect` |
| Drift analysis | `dan` | `description`, `algorithms`, `compute` |
| Ship identification | `shi` | `description`, `algorithms`, `identify` |
| Trajectory prediction | `trp` | `description`, `algorithms`, `predict` |

`/api/v1/technological_brick/algorithms` lists every registered algorithm
across all four bricks in one call. The full request/response schemas are
always up to date at `/api/v1/docs`.

## Testing

```bash
just test   # or: uv run pytest tests/
```
